function.name: generate_image_tool
function.description: Generates an image based on the provided description and saves it with the specified file name. The image description should be detailed to ensure the resulting image matches the desired subject and surroundings; otherwise, these aspects will be chosen randomly. This function is not intended for generating images from textual data. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

desc.description: A single string that provides a detailed description of the desired image. For example, 'a sunset over the mountains with a lake in the foreground'.

file_name.description: The name of the file to which the generated image will be saved. It should include the file extension, such as 'image.png'.

function.name: tts_tool
function.description: Converts the provided text content to speech and saves the resulting audio to a file. This function is intended for voice narration and should be used accordingly. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The text content that needs to be converted to speech.

speaker.description: The voice to be used for the text-to-speech conversion.

file_name.description: The name of the file to save the audio output without the extension. If left empty, a default name will be generated based on the content.

function.name: write_markdown_tool
function.description: Writes the provided content to a Markdown (.md) file on the disk. This function should be used when there is a need to persist text data in Markdown format as a result of a user action or a process that requires saving information in a structured text file. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The Markdown formatted text content to be written to the file.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the Markdown content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: write_html_tool
function.description: Writes an HTML file to disk with the given content. Ensures HTML tags within the content are properly closed. This function should be used when there is a need to save HTML content to a file as part of a 'save' operation. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

content.description: The HTML content to be written to the file. Must contain valid HTML structure.

filename.description: The name of the file to which the HTML content will be written. If not provided, a default filename will be used.

function.name: search_web_tool
function.description: Executes a search query using the DuckDuckGo search engine and returns a specified number of search results from a given source. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

query.description: The search term or phrase to be queried.

num_results.description: The maximum number of search results to return. A positive integer.

source.description: The source from which the search results should be fetched.

function.name: get_url_content
function.description: Scrapes the specified URL for textual data and returns the content as a string. This function is useful for extracting information from web pages when a URL is provided. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The web address of the page to scrape. It should be a valid URL format, such as 'http://www.example.com'.

timeout.description: The maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, with a default value that allows for a reasonable amount of time for most web pages to load.

user_agent.description: The User-Agent string to be used for the HTTP request to simulate a particular browser, which is optional. Some websites may require this for access.

message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** of how to create a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that:

* runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**  
* has **one NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU**  
* uses a standard machine type (you can swap it for a higher‑memory or higher‑CPU type if you wish)  
* is launched in a specific zone (replace `us-central1-a` with your preferred zone)  
* is named `rtx-a6000-ubuntu20`  

The example shows both the **REST API call** (via `curl`) and the equivalent **`gcloud` CLI** command.  
It also includes a short note on prerequisites (API enablement, billing, GPU quota, etc.).

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| Step | What to do | Why |
|------|------------|-----|
| **Enable Compute Engine API** | `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` | Needed for all Compute Engine operations. |
| **Enable GPU API** | `gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com` (same service) | GPUs are part of Compute Engine. |
| **Check GPU quota** | `gcloud compute accelerator-types list --filter="zone:us-central1-a"` | Ensure you have at least 1 A6000 available in the zone. |
| **Create a service account** (optional) | `gcloud iam service-accounts create rtx-sa --display-name="RTX A6000 SA"` | For fine‑grained IAM control. |
| **Grant the service account the Compute Admin role** | `gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding <PROJECT_ID> --member="serviceAccount:rtx-sa@<PROJECT_ID>.iam.gserviceaccount.com" --role="roles/compute.admin"` | Allows the SA to create instances. |
| **Authenticate** | `gcloud auth application-default login` | Provides an OAuth token for the REST call. |

> **Tip:** If you’re running the `curl` command from a machine that already has `gcloud` installed, you can obtain the access token with:
> ```bash
> ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)
> ```

---

## 2. REST API Call (curl)

```bash
# Variables – replace with your own values
PROJECT_ID="your-project-id"
ZONE="us-central1-a"
INSTANCE_NAME="rtx-a6000-ubuntu20"
MACHINE_TYPE="n1-standard-8"          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
GPU_TYPE="nvidia-tesla-a6000"
GPU_COUNT=1
IMAGE_PROJECT="ubuntu-os-cloud"
IMAGE_FAMILY="ubuntu-2004-lts"

# Get an access token
ACCESS_TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)

# Build the JSON body
read -r -d '' INSTANCE_BODY <<EOF
{
  "name": "$INSTANCE_NAME",
  "machineType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/machineTypes/$MACHINE_TYPE",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/$IMAGE_PROJECT/global/images/family/$IMAGE_FAMILY"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/acceleratorTypes/$GPU_TYPE",
      "acceleratorCount": $GPU_COUNT
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
EOF

# Make the API request
curl -X POST \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/$PROJECT_ID/zones/$ZONE/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ACCESS_TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d "$INSTANCE_BODY"
```

### What the JSON does

| Field | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `name` | Instance name |
| `machineType` | CPU/RAM configuration |
| `disks[0]` | Boot disk with Ubuntu 20.04 LTS |
| `networkInterfaces[0]` | Connects to the default VPC and gives an external IP |
| `guestAccelerators[0]` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `serviceAccounts[0]` | Grants the instance full Cloud Platform access |
| `metadata.items[0]` | Optional startup script to install the NVIDIA driver (you can omit or customize it) |

---

## 3. Equivalent `gcloud` CLI Command

If you prefer the CLI, the same instance can be created with a single command:

```bash
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu20 \
  --project=$PROJECT_ID \
  --zone=$ZONE \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --metadata startup-script='#!/bin/bash
sudo apt-get update
sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535' \
  --tags=http-server,https-server
```

> **Note:**  
> * `--boot-disk-size` and `--boot-disk-type` are optional; adjust as needed.  
> * The `--tags` flag is optional but useful if you plan to expose HTTP/HTTPS services.  
> * The startup script installs the NVIDIA driver; you can replace it with any custom script.

---

## 4. Quick Checklist

| ✅ | Item |
|----|------|
| [ ] Compute Engine API enabled |
| [ ] GPU quota available in chosen zone |
| [ ] Billing enabled for the project |
| [ ] OAuth token or service account with `compute.instances.create` permission |
| [ ] Correct machine type and GPU type |
| [ ] Proper image family (`ubuntu-2004-lts`) |
| [ ] Optional: startup script to install GPU drivers |

Once the instance is up, you can SSH into it and verify the GPU:

```bash
ssh rtx-a6000-ubuntu20@<EXTERNAL_IP>
nvidia-smi
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

---

### TL;DR

```bash
# REST API (curl)
curl -X POST "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<PROJECT_ID>/zones/<ZONE>/instances" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json
```

or

```bash
# gcloud CLI
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu20 \
  --project=<PROJECT_ID> \
  --zone=<ZONE> \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud
```

Replace `<PROJECT_ID>` and `<ZONE>` with your own values, and you’re good to go!
